listicles.title: 5 things to know before you buy a magnesium supplement
listicles.intro: Magnesium comes in a lot of forms and doses. Here's what to look at on the label, in plain words.

items.title: The form matters
items.body: Glycinate, citrate and oxide are the most common. Glycinate is usually described as gentle on the stomach; oxide contains more magnesium by weight but is absorbed less well.

items.title: Check the elemental dose
items.body: Labels should say how much actual magnesium is in a serving, not just the weight of the compound. Ours lists 200 mg per two capsules.

items.title: Timing is personal
items.body: Many people take magnesium in the evening as part of a wind-down routine. Taking it with food can help if your stomach is sensitive.

items.title: Pairing is common
items.body: Magnesium is often paired with L-theanine or ashwagandha in evening routines.

items.title: Ask first if you take medication
items.body: Magnesium can interact with some antibiotics and other medicines, and isn't right for everyone with kidney conditions. A pharmacist can check in a minute.

listicles.title: 6 signs your skin barrier needs a break (and a simple routine to try)
listicles.intro: Tight, stinging or suddenly flaky? Your routine may be doing too much. Here's what people with sensitive skin most often change first.

items.title: Your cleanser stings
items.body: A low-foam, fragrance-free gel cleanser is gentler than foaming washes with sulfates.

items.title: Skin feels tight after washing
items.body: That squeaky-clean feeling usually means too much has been stripped. Moisturise while skin is still damp.

items.title: Redness after new products
items.body: Pause actives (acids, retinoids) for a couple of weeks and go back to basics.

items.title: Dry patches that won't shift
items.body: Ceramide creams are designed to support the skin's own barrier lipids.

items.title: Everything feels dehydrated
items.body: A hyaluronic serum on damp skin, sealed with a cream, adds water-based hydration.

items.title: You skip sunscreen
items.body: Daily SPF protects stressed skin. Mineral filters are often better tolerated by sensitive skin.

advertorials.title: Why every Shelby tee and sweatshirt is printed after you order it
advertorials.dek: No warehouse full of unsold stock. Just the one you picked, made for you.

sections.p: Most clothing is made months ahead in big batches, and a lot of it is never sold. We wanted to do it differently.
When you order, a print partner prints your piece and ships it straight to you. It takes a few extra days, and nothing is wasted.
Because nothing is made in advance, we can offer a full size range without leftover stock.
If something arrives faulty or misprinted, we'll replace it.

advertorials.title: Printed for your home, made when you order
advertorials.dek: Mugs, prints and soft furnishings, each one made for the person who ordered it.

sections.p: Home pieces are personal, so we don't stack them in a warehouse. Each one is printed when it's ordered.

sections.h: Made by print partners near you
sections.p: Orders go to a print partner close to the delivery address where possible, which keeps shipping times reasonable.
Everything here is meant for everyday use, not just display. Care instructions are on each product page.
If something arrives damaged or misprinted, we'll replace it.

advertorials.title: Small things, made to order
advertorials.dek: Totes, caps and cases printed just for you, not pulled from a pile.

sections.p: Accessories are where a design really gets carried around, so we print each one when it's ordered.
Nothing is made in bulk, so a new design can arrive in the store the day it's ready.
Every product page lists materials and care, so you know what you're getting.
If something arrives faulty or misprinted, we'll replace it.

advertorials.title: Why we stopped recommending 10-step skincare routines
advertorials.dek: Our most common question is "what should I actually use?" Our answer got shorter.

sections.p: When we started building Shelby's skincare range, we read hundreds of questions from shoppers. The pattern was clear: people with irritated skin were often using more products, not fewer.
Dermatology guidance for sensitive and dry skin usually comes back to three steps: cleanse gently, moisturise, protect from the sun. So that's what we put together.

sections.h: Step 1: a cleanser that doesn't strip
sections.p: Low-foam and fragrance-free.

sections.h: Step 2: a cream that supports the barrier
sections.p: Ceramides, cholesterol and squalane, the same family of lipids your skin makes itself.
Zinc oxide with a sheer tint, so it doesn't leave a white cast.
If a product doesn't suit your skin, exchange it free within 30 days. Every product page lists the full ingredients.

advertorials.title: The evening routine our customers ask about most
advertorials.dek: It isn't complicated. That's probably why it sticks.

sections.p: Evening routines are one of the most common things shoppers ask us about. Most want something simple they'll actually keep doing.
Screens off a little earlier, a consistent bedtime, a cooler room. No supplement replaces these.
Many people add magnesium glycinate to their evening, often with L-theanine or ashwagandha. We stock both with full doses on the label.
If you're pregnant, nursing or on medication, ask your doctor or pharmacist first.
Not for you? Return it within 30 days for a full refund.
